intent: Increased sensor size to 0.016 m and shifted sensor positions forward by +0.01 m to improve early line detection and reduce line loss events, especially on the slalom track. Expect better progress and fewer line loss events, with smoother steering and improved finish rates.
rationale: The race data shows good completion and progress on oval and s-bend tracks but poor performance on the slalom, with frequent line loss events (1.05 on slalom) and no finishes. Steering oscillation is moderate to high, especially on s-bend (0.47) and slalom (0.38). Integration feedback suggests increasing sensor size to 0.016 m to improve line coverage and reduce line loss, and shifting sensor positions forward by +0.01 m to detect the line earlier, which may help with progress and reduce oscillation. The current sensor layout is five sensors evenly spaced at y=0.04-0.05 m; moving them forward to y=0.05-0.06 m should improve early detection. We keep the same number of sensors and lateral spacing to maintain resolution. Wheel track, radius, body size, and mass remain unchanged to preserve stability and handling. The intent is to reduce line loss events, especially on challenging tracks, and improve progress and finish rates by better early line detection and coverage. We request measurements including completion, progress, line_loss_events, rms_error, steering_oscillation, and control_effort to evaluate improvements and control smoothness.
